questions.stem: Let f(x) = 1 if x ≥ 5, and f(x) = 0 otherwise. What is f(3) + f(7) + f(5)?
questions.explain: f(3) = 0, f(7) = 1 and f(5) = 1 because the rule says x ≥ 5 includes 5. The sum is 2.

questions.stem: The rows of X are samples and the columns are features: X = $\begin{pmatrix}5&2\\1&8\\7&3\end{pmatrix}$. Which samples have a feature 2 (column 2) value above 2.5?
questions.explain: Column 2 is (2, 8, 3). Only 8 and 3 exceed 2.5, and they are in rows 2 and 3.

questions.stem: Of 10 emails, 4 are spam. Of the 4 spam emails, 3 contain the word “free”, and of the 6 other emails, 1 does. Given that an email contains “free”, what is the probability that it is spam?
questions.explain: Only emails containing “free” matter: 3 spam plus 1 non-spam is 4 emails. Of these, 3 are spam, so the probability is 3/4 = 0.75.
